newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slip as Lek runs out of steam.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slip as Lek runs out of steam.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 1.06 percent on Friday and traders said the market would most likely track sideways next week as the feverish buying of the new issue of Lek shares seemed to have run out of steam.
"Lek fell today which could mean that its share price has already reached its peak. That may be a slightly inhibiting factor for the market," one broker said.
Since being listed on Wednesday last week, Lek's A shares have surged 18.1 percent, although they eased 1.72 percent today.
* The seven-share SBI index fell 9.86 points to 918.86.
* 13 shares fell and three rose, while eight were untraded.
* Turnover eased to 124.2 million tolars from 127.7 million.
* Lek's A shares were the most actively traded, falling 1.72 percent to 16.000 on volume of 5,649 shares for total turnover of 90.3 million tolars.
* Ordinary shares of bank Hipotekarna banka Brezice were the leading decliners, tumbling 9.7 percent to 2,958 on volume of 143 shares for total turnover of 0.4 million tolars.
* Bank SKB was the top gainer, rising 3.78 percent to 24,255 on volume of 163 shares for total turnover of 4 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
